source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU procurement)
why_relevant: EU-threshold tenders from Hungarian state financial bodies appear here in structured, multilingual form. Contract notices and award notices for banking IT, core-system, consultancy and HR/staffing services expose transformation programmes and their suppliers.

source_name: MFB – Magyar Fejlesztési Bank Zrt. corporate site (sajtószoba / közérdekű adatok)
why_relevant: State development bank; publishes its own leadership appointments, board composition and mandatory 'közérdekű adatok' (organisational and personnel data). Directly on-topic for leadership moves and org changes.

source_name: EXIM (Eximbank Zrt. / MEHIB Zrt.) corporate site
why_relevant: State export credit bank and export credit insurer under ministerial ownership control; CEO appointments are made by the minister and announced here and in the gazette (e.g. the July 2026 CEO change). Also a hiring source via its career page.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár (Hungarian State Treasury) – Vezetőség / szervezet pages
why_relevant: MÁK is a major retail government-securities distributor and payments/accounting infrastructure operator. Its published leadership list (president, elnökhelyettesek) and organisational chart change with each SZMSZ revision — a clean, diffable signal of org change and leadership moves.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Menedzsment / Szervezeti-személyzeti adatok
why_relevant: Magyar Posta operates a large financial-services arm (postal payments, agency banking, Posta Biztosító). It publishes a dated PDF of the company's leaders and a statutory szervezeti/személyzeti adatok page — an unusually explicit, versioned record of executive changes.

source_name: Diákhitel Központ Zrt. (student loan agency) – official site
why_relevant: State-owned lender; its CEO changes are announced publicly and are a recurring channel for senior banking-sector people moving between OTP/MKB/MFB and state institutions — good for building the executive-mobility graph.

source_name: MNV Zrt. (Hungarian National Asset Management) – közérdekű adatok
why_relevant: The state's asset manager: its portfolio lists and board-nomination records identify which financial entities are state-controlled and who sits on their boards. A pointer that keeps the actor map for this cell current as ownership moves between MNV, ministries and holding vehicles.

source_name: Közadatkereső / közadattár (unified public-interest data search, operated by NISZ)
why_relevant: Central index of statutory public-interest data publications by public-duty organisations. Its 'szervezeti és személyzeti adatok' category is exactly the org-chart and leadership disclosure required by law — one crawl point covering many state financial bodies at once.

source_name: KÖZIGÁLLÁS / Közszolgálati állásportál (public-service job portal)
why_relevant: Statutory publication venue for vacancies at public-administration employers, including the State Treasury and other state financial bodies. Job titles and unit names in the ads are a direct read on hiring volume and on newly created organisational units. Note: legacy domain kozigallas.gov.hu appears to have been superseded.

source_name: Kormany.hu – government / ministry press releases (NGM, ministerial ownership decisions)
why_relevant: The minister exercising ownership rights (currently the economy/energy portfolio) announces CEO appointments at Eximbank, MEHIB, MFB and treasury leadership here, often before or alongside the gazette. Also announces institutional mergers and mandate transfers.

source_name: Állami Számvevőszék (ÁSZ) – audit reports on state financial institutions
why_relevant: State audit reports on MFB, Eximbank, MÁK and postal financial services describe governance structures, staffing, IT outsourcing and organisational deficiencies in detail — slow-moving but exceptionally substantive context for org-change analysis.

source_name: Portfolio.hu – bank section (state-institution leadership coverage)
why_relevant: Fastest reliable secondary reporting on Hungarian banking leadership changes, including state institutions (e.g. the Diákhitel Központ CEO change). Useful as an early trigger to then go find the authoritative gazette/Cégközlöny record.

source_name: Világgazdaság / VG.hu – state-institution appointments coverage
why_relevant: Business daily that reliably carries ministry-sourced appointment announcements for state banks (EXIM, MFB, Diákhitel) with the ministerial framing and mandate description, which the gazette entry itself omits.

source_name: 424/2017. (XII. 19.) Korm. rendelet on electronic public procurement (Jogtár)
why_relevant: Defines what must be published where in EKR and the Közbeszerzési Értesítő, and the exemptions. Reading it tells the collection design which state-entity contracts are guaranteed to be visible and which are legally allowed to stay dark — essential for interpreting silence.

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. — investor relations / sajtószoba (regulated disclosures + press releases)
why_relevant: 4iG is the dominant Hungarian IT integrator and a listed issuer, so it must publish contract wins, subsidiary reorganisations and management appointments. Its financial-sector engagements and named executive changes are an indirect read-through to bank programme teams and org changes that the private banks themselves never disclose.

source_name: BÉT (Budapest Stock Exchange) issuer disclosure page — 4iG Nyrt.
why_relevant: Mandatory disclosure channel: board/management changes at the largest bank-serving integrator arrive here first and dated. Also carries the semi-annual and quarterly reports whose segment commentary names financial-sector contracts.

source_name: ANY Biztonsági Nyomda Nyrt. — corporate site / press & investor pages
why_relevant: Listed Hungarian security printer doing plastic card production and personalisation plus bulk transactional print for banks. Its announcements and management changes are a proxy signal for card-portfolio and statement-outsourcing programmes at private banks, and for card-issuing reorganisation.

source_name: CARDNET Zrt. — corporate site (POS estate operator for Hungarian banks)
why_relevant: Operates roughly 50-65k POS terminals nationwide as an outsourced arm of bank acquiring operations, and heads the Cardnet/Festipay/Cellum group. Its client references, service-launch news and management pages expose which banks outsource terminal operations and when those bank-side teams change.

source_name: Profession.hu employer profile pages for bank-serving vendors (e.g. CARDNET Zrt.)
why_relevant: Hungary's main local job board. Vendor vacancy text names the client bank programme, the technology stack and the team being built — the most direct visible proxy for a private bank's undisclosed programme staffing.

source_name: Bitport.hu — Hungarian enterprise-IT trade portal
why_relevant: Covers core-banking replacements and integrator contracts with named vendors and named bank CIOs — e.g. its reporting on MKB Bank's core system switch to Oracle Flexcube. Also runs CIO Hungary/CIO Budapest, whose speaker lists are a de-facto directory of current bank IT leadership.

source_name: ITBusiness.hu — Hungarian ICT business magazine (print PDF archive included)
why_relevant: Carries vendor-supplied appointment announcements (country manager, régióvezető) and bank-IT project features that name integrators and their bank customers. Its downloadable issue PDFs make historical appointment tracking feasible.

source_name: EPA / OSZK Elektronikus Periodika Archívum — ITBusiness back issues
why_relevant: National library archive of Hungarian ICT trade press. Gives a stable, fetchable PDF backfile for reconstructing multi-year vendor country-lead appointment history and bank project timelines when publisher sites rotate URLs.

source_name: MINDSPIRE — Hungarian core-banking transformation consultancy (blog + service pages)
why_relevant: Publishes recurring status reviews of Hungarian core-banking renewal projects and names the platforms in play (Flexcube, T24, Murex, CAMS, SMAC). Effectively a curated map of which private bank is running which programme and with which vendor — the best single pointer into this cell.

source_name: Finshape (ex-W.UP + BSC) — vendor site and Hungarian press coverage
why_relevant: Czech-Hungarian digital-banking vendor with a Budapest entity and named bank clients (Raiffeisen, Erste, BNP Paribas, Société Générale). Its named Hungary-client lead and merger-driven reorganisation are exactly the vendor-side org signal this cell targets.

source_name: Portfolio.hu vendor tag pages (e.g. /cimke/finshape, 4iG coverage)
why_relevant: Portfolio is the leading HU business daily and maintains per-company tag streams. Tag pages give a low-cost persistent watch on each bank-supplier entity, including contract, ownership and executive-departure stories the vendors do not self-publish.

source_name: Nexi Central Europe — corporate site and newsroom (CEE processing hub incl. Hungary)
why_relevant: Nexi Central Europe is the group's CEE competence centre for ATM/POS management and issuing/acquiring processing and stood up Nexi Central Europe in Hungary. Announcements of new bank processing mandates and of local country leadership are a direct pointer to card-operations reorganisation inside HU banks.

source_name: Tietoevry Banking newsroom — Hungary bank references
why_relevant: Published the completion of OTP Bank Hungary's card-acquiring software replacement — the archetypal 'vendor announces what the bank will not' item. Such releases date the programme and often name the bank-side owner, revealing the card/payments org structure.

source_name: FinTech Futures — core-banking vendor-win reporting (CEE/Hungary)
why_relevant: Trade outlet that reports vendor selections before either side issues a full release — e.g. OTP Bank tapping Intellect/iGCB for a core revamp. Useful as an early-warning layer over vendor newsrooms for HU bank programme starts.
